source.title: UnlearningSoup: Is Repeated Tuning Necessary for Large Language Model Unlearning?
source.authors: Pu-Ning Yang; Qi-Zhou Wang; Jun-Chi Yu; Bo Han; Xiu-Ying Chen

record.tranche_reason: It evaluates relearning, cross-lingual, and jailbreak attacks on unlearned models using different robustness measurements; it does not test the claim’s specific fine-tuning-on-unrelated-examples, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompt-rephrasing procedures.
record.gate_note: Attack outcomes are reported in Table 10 and Table 11. The paper also discusses attacks and unlearning robustness in related-work sections, but those cited findings are not recorded as rows. Main unlearning-quality tables are not rows for these versions because they do not measure recovery under an attack.
record.test_reason: The paper is a model-selection method (weight souping), but its robustness check (Tables 10–11, App. E.5) reports how much forgotten knowledge resurfaces under relearning, French translation and jailbreak prompts. This covers baseline unlearned models and souped ones, which bears on versions B and E. UnlearningSoup does not claim to resist these attacks; it is only reported as 'comparable' to tuning, so it is not an F counter-method.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors say UnlearningSoup models are about as robust as tuning-selected models. Cross-lingual and jailbreak attacks barely move the results. Relearning is much more aggressive, and souping may improve or weaken it depending on over- or under-unlearning. On MUSE-Books they report robustness comparable to tuning-based models.
record.recipe_differences: UnlearningSoup interpolates or reweights candidate unlearned model weights; the evaluated attacks include cross-lingual translation, one-epoch relearning on the unlearning data, and jailbreak prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type changes the measured outcome; relearning causes much larger changes than cross-lingual or jailbreak conditions. The attack outcomes also vary by method and soup-selection strategy.
record.problems: The attack evaluations cover a limited model and dataset setting in the reported detailed results. No uncertainty estimates are given for attack-table values. The tested relearning procedure uses the forgotten data directly and does not establish recovery from unrelated or loosely related examples. EQ is an aggregate forgetting measure rather than a direct recovered-knowledge accuracy comparison against a model that never saw the knowledge.
record.rows_left_out: None. The selected MUSE attack rows cover EfficientSoup; Table 11 also reports PerformanceSoup values, omitted because the 60-row limit was reached after retaining both attack and no-attack results for the six methods under EfficientSoup. Other robustness details are shown in Figure 6 and Table 10.

untested.parts: No comparison to chance or to a never-trained model, and no WMDP attack test. Its prompt-attack results are recorded under E rather than A.
Only one epoch on the full forget set; no small, unrelated, loosely related or subset relearning sets; no WMDP.
No activation ablation or internal analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Only French translation and two DAN-style persona prompts on TOFU with LLaMA-3.2-3B. No rephrasing, in-context information or other languages.
UnlearningSoup is a model-selection method that does not claim attack resistance; no robust counter-method is tested.

missing.what: Tuning-based (non-soup) and PerformanceSoup columns for MUSE-Books relearning, e.g. NPO tuned VerbMem 10.4→68.6. The tuning-based omission is not declared in rows_left_out.
Pre-unlearning reference values needed to size recovery: MUSE-Books original VerbMem 99.56 / KnowMem 58.32; TOFU-10% LLaMA-3.2-3B original EQ 0.1578.

record.verdict_notes: The attack evaluation is a secondary robustness check in a model-selection paper, and no uncertainty is reported. Relearning uses the whole forget set, the strongest and least informative form of B. The TOFU EQ aggregate and the MUSE ROUGE-based memorization measures give very different pictures of relearning recovery. Version codes V1/V2/V3/V6 in the record were invalid and have been remapped.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish near-chance targeted accuracy with preserved general ability and then test whether the named attacks recover knowledge relative to a never-trained model.
Tests one epoch of relearning on the unlearning data, not a few unrelated or loosely related examples or a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit test.
Tests cross-lingual and jailbreak conditions, not rephrasing alone, other in-context information, or all languages.
UnlearningSoup is evaluated under the paper’s three attack settings; it is not tested against every attack named in the claim.

source_check.notes: Table 10 is column-scrambled but readable. Its 'Original' row is the unlearned model with no attack; the pre-unlearning EQ is 0.1578. Relearning is one epoch on the full forget set, with no retrain or retrain+relearn control. The two jailbreak prompts (quoted attack prompts, not injections) share one row. Table 11's tuning-based W/ relearning values are given to 2 decimals, and the text doesn't say where they come from.
